preamble: 1. ข้อสอบมีทั้งหมด 100 ข้อ
2. ข้อสอบเป็นอังกฤษทั้งหมด
3. มีเวลาในการสอบ 2 ชั่วโมง 30 นาที

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being stabbed in the right hypochondriac region, just below the right costal margin at the midclavicular line. At surgery, an organ located on the inferior surface of the liver is found to be perforated, with bile leaking into the peritoneal cavity. Which organ was most likely injured?
A patient with liver cirrhosis presents with caput medusae around the umbilicus. This condition is caused by dilation of which vein?
A 2-year-old boy presents with a painless lump in the scrotum that increases in size when he cries. Which of the following conditions is most likely associated with this finding?
A 35-year-old man was stabbed at right hypochondriac region. Which organ would be most likely injured?

A 50-year-old woman with a long history of heartburn develops severe epigastric pain and is urgently admitted to the hospital. Gastroscopic examination reveals a small perforated ulcer on the posterior wall of the body of the stomach. At surgery, with the patient in the supine position, 150 mL of blood-tinged, frothy gray fluid is aspirated from the peritoneal cavity. Where would this fluid most likely collect first?
Bleeding at the umbilical ligament region is most commonly caused by injury to which structure?
After inguinal hernia repair, a patient has loss of sensation over the anterior scrotum, while the cremasteric reflex is intact. Which nerve was most likely injured?

choices.A: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve

questions.stem: During an open abdominal surgery for severe liver trauma, the surgeon inserts a finger behind the free edge of the lesser omentum and compresses the structures within the hepatoduodenal ligament to control bleeding (Pringle maneuver). While the finger is in place, a large vessel is palpated posterior to the finger. Which structure is most likely located posterior to the surgeon’s finger?

During retroperitoneal surgery, the left renal vein is ligated proximal to its junction with the inferior vena cava. Venous blood from the left testis must therefore drain through an alternative pathway. Which vessel will most likely carry this venous blood?
A patient develops an anterior abdominal wall hematoma after blunt trauma to the upper abdomen. Which vessel is the most likely source of bleeding?

During surgery for a perforated duodenal ulcer, the surgeon ligates a vessel arising from the gastroduodenal artery that runs along the greater curvature of the stomach and supplies the right portion of the stomach. Which vessel was ligated?

A 55-year-old man undergoes surgical exposure of the inferior vena cava (IVC) near the liver for tumor resection. During the procedure, the surgeon wants to avoid injuring structures that could cause autonomic dysfunction of the upper gastrointestinal tract. Which structure should the surgeon be most careful to preserve?

A 45-year-old man reports an urge to defecate shortly after eating a large meal. This is caused by a powerful colonic contraction that propels fecal material from the transverse colon toward the rectum. Which of the following mechanisms is primarily responsible for this process?

A 40-year-old man complains of mid-epigastric pain that is relieved by antacids. Endoscopy shows gastric mucosal hypertrophy. Which of the following hormones is most likely responsible for this condition?
A 45-year-old man eats a high-fat meal. Which of the following hormones is most responsible for stimulating gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion to aid fat digestion?
A patient starts salivating and his stomach begins secreting acid when he thinks about his favorite meal. This phase of gastric secretion is known as:

A 24-year-old woman has dinner at 7 PM and then goes to sleep. The next morning, before breakfast, she notices rumbling sounds in her upper abdomen. Her physician explains that these sounds are caused by strong, cyclic contractions moving residual food and secretions through the small intestine. Which phase of gastrointestinal motility is responsible for this phenomenon?
A 28-year-old woman finishes a large breakfast and, within 20 minutes, feels an urgent need to defecate. Strong contractions move fecal matter toward the rectum. Which reflex is responsible?

A 35-year-old man with recurrent peptic ulcers undergoes a surgical procedure to cut the nerve that stimulates gastric acid secretion when he thinks about food. After surgery, his stomach acid secretion is significantly reduced. Which procedure did he undergo?

A 30-year-old man eats a mixed meal. In his small intestine, strong, rhythmic contractions occur that mix chyme with digestive enzymes and bile, bringing it into contact with the intestinal mucosa for absorption. Which type of intestinal motility is primarily responsible?

A 5-year-old child with acute diarrhea is given oral rehydration solution (ORS) containing glucose and sodium. Through which mechanism is glucose absorbed in the small intestine, helping water reabsorption?

choices.E: Active transport of glucose independent of sodium

questions.stem: A fibrous structure lies on the surface of the liver. One end is connected to the inferior vena cava (IVC) and the other end is connected to the left branch of the portal vein. This structure is a remnant of which embryologic vessel?

A 32-year-old American tourist visits Thailand for the first time. Two days after eating street food, he develops profuse watery diarrhea without blood, abdominal cramping, and mild nausea. Which of the following mechanisms most likely explains his diarrhea?

choices.D: Osmotic retention of water from undigested carbohydrates

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presents with diffuse bone pain and difficulty climbing stairs due to proximal muscle weakness. He reports minimal sun exposure and a diet low in dairy products. Laboratory tests reveal low serum calcium and elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH). Which vitamin deficiency is most likely responsible for his symptoms?

A 32-year-old woman presents with fatigue, pallor, numbness and tingling in her hands and feet. Laboratory tests show macrocytic anemia and hypersegmented neutrophils. She follows a strict vegan diet and has had no animal product intake for several years. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely?
A 30-year-old man fasts and drinks only water for 2 days. He feels weak and hungry. Which metabolic pathway is predominantly providing glucose for his body during this period?

A 30-year-old man receives glucose orally and intravenously on separate occasions. Plasma glucose rises faster after IV administration, but insulin levels spike higher after oral glucose. Which mechanism best explains this phenomenon?

choices.A: Faster glucose absorption in the gut
choices.C: Release of gastrointestinal hormones (GIP and GLP-1)
choices.D: Direct stimulation of pancreatic alpha cells
choices.E: Slower renal clearance of oral glucose

questions.stem: After a meal, the “acid tide” (acidic chyme entering the duodenum) stimulates the pancreatic duct to secrete bicarbonate. Which hormone primarily mediates this process?

A 45-year-old man comes to the clinic because he has noticed dark urine for 2 weeks. He denies abdominal pain or fever. Laboratory tests reveal elevated conjugated bilirubin. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his jaundice?

A 45-year-old man undergoes surgical resection of the terminal ileum for Crohn’s disease. Weeks later, he develops fatty, foul-smelling stools that are difficult to flush. Which of the following complications is most likely responsible?

A 28-year-old woman at 8 weeks’ gestation presents with mild to moderate nausea and occasional vomiting. She has no signs of dehydration. Which of the following is the first-line therapy for her symptoms?
A patient develops extrapyramidal symptoms including akathisia, dystonia, and tremor after taking an antiemetic. Which drug is most likely responsible?
A 48-year-old man presents with mild fatigue. He drinks alcohol socially. Labs show: AST: 85 U/L ALT: 45 U/L GGT: 150 U/L Which of the following patterns does this most likely indicate?
Which of the following lab patterns is most consistent with long-standing hypertension? AST ALT Albumin ALP Bilirubin

A 52-year-old man presents with fatigue, nausea, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and jaundice for 5 days. No history of chronic liver disease. He drinks alcohol occasionally. Laboratory results show: Total bilirubin: 4.0 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 2.5 mg/dL AST: 850 U/L ALT: 920 U/L ALP: 140 U/L Albumin: 4.3 g/dL What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents with GERD, reporting heartburn, regurgitation, and epigastric discomfort. The refluxed gastric acid irritates her esophagus. Which of the following is the primary esophageal response triggered by the acidic reflux?

choices.D: Transient relaxation of the upper esophageal sphincter
choices.E: Permanent contraction of the lower esophageal sphincter

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient undergoes resection of the ileum due to Crohn’s disease. Which of the following changes is most likely to occur after this surgery?

A 12-year-old girl presents with poor weight gain, greasy stools, and recurrent sinus infections. Sweat chloride test and genetic analysis confirm cystic fibrosis. Which of the following is most likely increased in her pancreatic secretions?
A 40-year-old man presents with mid-epigastric discomfort, which is relieved by antacids. Endoscopy shows gastric mucosal hypertrophy. Which hormone is most likely responsible for this condition?

A 50-year-old man presents with sudden onset of massive vomiting of bright red blood. On physical examination, he has ascites and splenomegaly. Serologic testing shows HBcAg positive. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his hematemesis?

A 55-year-old man has been taking NSAIDs daily for chronic osteoarthritis for several months. He complains of mild epigastric discomfort, which improves after taking antacids. Which of the following changes is most likely to occur in his stomach?

choices.A: Decreased prostaglandin synthesis leading to reduced mucus and bicarbonate secretion.
choices.B: Increased gastrin secretion causing hypertrophy of gastric folds.
choices.C: Hyperplasia of parietal cells with increased hydrochloric acid production.
choices.D: Autoimmune destruction of parietal cells resulting in achlorhydria.
choices.E: Increased lower esophageal sphincter tone due to enhanced vagal activity.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy complains of nausea, vomiting, and mild epigastric discomfort. She reports that symptoms are worse in the morning and improve slightly after eating. Which of the following gastrointestinal conditions is she most likely experiencing?

A 60-year-old man has had progressive difficulty swallowing over the past 6 months. Endoscopy reveals erythematous mucosa 3 cm above the esophagogastric junction. Biopsy shows intestinal metaplasia. Which of the following is the most likely long-term consequence?

A 40-year-old man has had epigastric pain for more than 1 year, occurring after meals and relieved by antacids. Endoscopy shows chronic atrophic gastritis of the gastric body. Rapid urease test is positive. If he does not receive treatment, which of the following complications is most likely to develop?
A 45-year-old obese woman has experienced epigastric burning after meals for more than 1 year. Endoscopy shows hyperemia and erosion of the lower esophageal mucosa. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman in her third trimester of pregnancy experiences increasing pain during defecation and notices fresh blood on the stool. She has no previous gastrointestinal problems. After giving birth, her symptoms improve and there is no rectal bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?

A 35-year-old woman underwent appendectomy 6 months ago. She now presents with intermittent crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and occasional vomiting. Bowel movements are irregular. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
A patient presents with severe watery diarrhea. Laboratory testing confirms cholera toxin positive. Which of the following transporters is primarily involved in this symptom?
A 51-year-old man constantly feels bloated and has dyspepsia after meals. Which of the following reflexes is most likely responsible for his discomfort?
A 28-year-old man develops watery diarrhea a few hours after eating street-vended fried rice while traveling. The diarrhea is caused by a bacterium that increases intestinal secretion of which ion?
Make a diagnosis based on the image.
Make a diagnosis based on the image.
Make a diagnosis based on the image.
Make a diagnosis based on the image.
A 30-year-old man develops fever, periorbital edema, and muscle pain 2 weeks after eating undercooked pork. Which stage of Trichinella spiralis is responsible for his muscle symptoms?

A 35-year-old man presents with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice. Ultrasound shows biliary obstruction, and history reveals he recently consumed undercooked pork. Which of the following parasites is the most likely cause of biliary infection?
A 7-year-old child presents with perianal itching, especially at night. The physician performs a scotch tape test to collect samples. Which of the following organisms is most likely detected?
The characteristic of this parasite found in a patient’s stool are rhabditiform larvae with a large genital primordium. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
A person develops itching and a rash on the feet after walking barefoot on contaminated soil. Which of the following parasites is most likely responsible?
What is the parasites from the picture?

A 3-year-old boy always plays with his dog. 2 weeks ago, he developed cutaneous larva migrans on his foot. No parasite eggs were found in the boy’s feces, but eggs were found in the dog’s feces. Which of the following type of parasite is involved in this case?
A 40-year-old man presents with fatigue, pallor, and numbness in the hands and feet. He reports a history of eating raw freshwater fish regularly. What is disease?
Which of the following is the most likely source of infection?

A 55-year-old man presents with severe diarrhea and significant weight loss for 1 week. He reports a history of eating uncooked freshwater fish. Stool examination demonstrates thick- walled eggs with two flattened plugs at each end. Which of the following is the most likely causative parasite?

A 2-year-old boy presents with fever, vesicular rashes on his hands, feet, and oral mucosa. Over the past 2 days, he develops difficulty breathing and lethargy. Which of the following pathogens is most likely associated with this severe complication?
Which of the following is the most concerning disadvantage of oral polio vaccine (OPV) administration?

choices.D: Reversion of vaccine to wild type virus

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man, who had a history of paralytic poliomyelitis in childhood, presents with gradual weakness, muscle atrophy, and fatigue in previously affected limbs. These symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past several years. Which of the following mechanisms best explains his current muscle weakness?

choices.C: Chronic infection in central nervous system

questions.stem: A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester presents with jaundice, fatigue, and dark urine for 5 days. She lives in a rural area with limited access to clean water. Laboratory tests show elevated AST/ALT and mild hyperbilirubinemia. Which of the following viruses is most likely responsible for her condition and is associated with high risk of stillbirth?
Blood cultures reveal a Gram-positive rod that can grow at 4°C. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
A 7-year-old child presents with diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. The stool culture grows Campylobacter jejuni. Which of the following is the most likely source of infection?

choices.E: Hand-to-mouth transmission from a healthy adult

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presents with fever, abdominal cramps, and bloody diarrhea 2 days after eating undercooked chicken. Stool culture reveals a gram-negative bacillus that is non- lactose fermenting on MacConkey agar and produces hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) on triple sugar iron (TSI) agar. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this infection?
A man develops severe abdominal pain and watery diarrhea within 6 hours after eating reheated rice. Which organism is most likely responsible?

A 35-year-old man develops profuse watery diarrhea without blood or mucus one day after eating raw vegetables contaminated with fecal matter while traveling in a developing country. He has no fever, and stool examination shows no leukocytes. Which of the following toxins is most likely responsible for his condition?
Which of the following organisms is a common cause of traveler’s diarrhea?

A 6-year-old boy presents with bloody diarrhea for 3 days after eating undercooked beef. Two days later, he develops fatigue, pallor, decreased urine output, and facial edema. Laboratory studies reveal: Hemoglobin: decreased Platelet count: decreased Serum creatinine: elevated Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this condition?
Which of the following hepatic cell types would be most increased in activity to help clear the offending agent?
Despite living in a highly acidic environment, the organism is able to survive in the stomach. Which of the following mechanisms most likely allows this organism to survive in gastric acid?

choices.A: Production of catalase to neutralize reactive oxygen species
choices.B: Formation of a protective polysaccharide capsule
choices.E: Increased thickness of bacterial cell wall

questions.stem: Stool culture demonstrates a non–lactose-fermenting gram-negative bacillus that produces a potent cytotoxin inhibiting protein synthesis. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this condition?

A 32-year-old man with advanced HIV infection presents with chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, and abdominal cramps for several weeks. Stool examination reveals round oocysts that require modified acid-fast staining for visualization. Which of the following protozoa is the most likely cause of this infection?

A 50-year-old man with a history of peptic ulcer disease presents with recurrent epigastric pain. He is prescribed omeprazole as part of his treatment regimen to reduce gastric acid secretion. What is the primary mechanism of action of this drug?

choices.A: Competitive inhibition of histamine H₂ receptors on parietal cells
choices.B: Neutralization of gastric acid by buffering action
choices.C: Inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis in gastric mucosa
choices.D: Irreversible inhibition of the H⁺/K⁺-ATPase proton pump

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy presents with an intensely pruritic, serpiginous erythematous rash on his foot that has been slowly migrating over several days. His parents report that he frequently walks barefoot on the beach. The diagnosis of cutaneous larva migrans is made. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 38-year-old man develops severe chronic watery diarrhea following resection of the distal ileum due to traumatic abdominal injury. The diarrhea is caused by impaired enterohepatic circulation of bile acids. Which of the following drugs is most appropriate for treating this condition based on its pathology?

A 29-year-old woman has recurrent abdominal pain associated with frequent loose stools for the past 6 months. Symptoms are relieved after defecation and worsen with stress. Physical examination and routine laboratory tests are normal. Colonoscopy shows no structural abnormality. She is diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhea predominant (IBS-D). Which of the following medications is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient?

A 42-year-old man from an endemic area presents with chronic swelling of the lower extremities, skin thickening, and recurrent episodes of fever. Peripheral blood smear demonstrates microfilariae. He is diagnosed with lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis). Which of the following medications is the most appropriate treatment for this condition?

27-year-old woman presents with recurrent crampy abdominal pain associated with changes in bowel habits for the past 8 months. The pain is relieved after defecation and worsens during periods of stress. Physical examination and laboratory studies are unremarkable. She is diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Which of the following medications is most appropriate for relieving her abdominal pain?

A 25-year-old man presents with chronic foul-smelling diarrhea, bloating, and weight loss for several weeks after drinking untreated stream water. Stool examination reveals pear- shaped flagellated protozoa. He prefers a treatment regimen that requires the shortest duration and single-dose administration. Which of the following medications is the most appropriate treatment?

A 6-year-old boy presents with perianal itching at night. Stool examination confirms infection with an intestinal nematode. The patient is treated with a drug that causes neuromuscular blockade of the parasite, leading to paralysis and expulsion in stool. Which of the following medications has this mechanism of action?

An obese patient presents with dark, thickened, velvety hyperpigmentation around the neck and axillae. Laboratory studies suggest metabolic abnormalities. This skin condition is most commonly associated with which of the following underlying mechanisms?

A 62-year-old man develops watery diarrhea after receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics. Colonoscopy reveals yellow-white pseudomembranes. Infection with Clostridioides difficile is suspected. Which of the following laboratory the best method is used to detect toxin A and toxin B produced by this organism?

A 12-year-old child has a strong family history of obesity and metabolic syndrome. Nutritional counseling is provided to reduce the child’s future risk of obesity. Which of the following dietary components is most strongly associated with increased risk of obesity and should be limited in this child?

A newborn infant develops bleeding around the umbilical stump shortly after birth. There is no history of trauma. Physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. Deficiency of which of the following is the most likely cause of this condition?
A 28-year-old female develops chronic diarrhea and bloating after eating wheat products. Symptoms improve when she avoids these foods. Which dietary component is most likely responsible?

A 25-year-old male experiences bloating, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea shortly after consuming milk, sugar-free gum, or fruit juice. Symptoms resolve when he avoids these foods. Which type of carbohydrate is most likely responsible?

choices.E: Disaccharides fully hydrolyzed by intestinal enzymes

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male presents with progressive abdominal distension and mild lower limb edema. He has a history of hypertension and mild heart disease. Laboratory investigations show: Serum albumin: 3.8 g/dL Serum total protein: 7.5 g/dL Ascitic fluid albumin: 2.5 g/dL Ascitic fluid total protein: 1.5 g/dL Which of the following is the most likely cause of his ascites?

A 62-year-old male with alcoholic liver disease presents with acute onset abdominal pain and fever. Laboratory investigations show: SAAG: 1.9 g/dL (high) Serum total protein: 7.0 g/dL Which of the following is the most likely cause of his ascites?

A 62-year-old male with a history of chronic liver disease presents with abdominal distension, mild fever, and generalized malaise for 2 days. He denies vomiting or jaundice. Laboratory investigations show: Serum albumin: 3.5 g/dL Ascitic fluid albumin: 2.8 g/dL SAAG: 0.7 g/dL Ascitic fluid appearance: Slightly cloudy Ascitic fluid ADA: 120 U/L

A 45-year-old male presents with severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. On examination, his abdomen is tender in the epigastric region. Laboratory tests show mildly elevated liver enzymes (AST 85 U/L, ALT 90 U/L) and total bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL. Which of the following enzymes is most specific for diagnosing the underlying condition?
